name: Jadeite
physical: Traditionally associated with long life and wellbeing
Said to bring a calm, balanced feeling
Folk tradition links it with comfort and resilience
summary: Jadeite is the rarest and most valuable true jade, famed for emerald-green Imperial colour and linked with luck, serenity and refined prosperity.
intro: Jadeite is the rarer of the two minerals sold as jade, and it is the stone behind the most expensive jade jewelry in the world. It is a sodium aluminium pyroxene that forms in high-pressure metamorphic rocks, creating a tightly interlocked mass of tiny crystals that is outstandingly tough. Colours include apple green, lavender, white, orange, black and the legendary intense emerald hue known as Imperial. Translucent stones show a gentle inner glow. Compared with nephrite, jadeite is slightly harder and has a glassier shine. High-grade cabochons and bangles are valued by collectors and jewelers worldwide.
history: Jadeite was used in Mesoamerica long before its Asian story began: the Olmec and Maya carved blue-green jadeite into masks, beads and ritual objects, and prized it above gold. In Asia, jadeite arrived later than nephrite. Burmese jadeite began to flow into China in large amounts during the eighteenth century, and quickly became the stone of the Qing court, especially in rich translucent green. The mineral was only identified as distinct from nephrite in 1863 by the French chemist Alexis Damour. Myanmar's Hpakant district remains the main source for the finest stones, and Guatemala has a growing production.
meaning: In crystal tradition jadeite is a refined stone of serenity, good fortune and heart-centred success. Practitioners say it encourages harmony within the family, protects travellers and brings a graceful approach to wealth. Its green colours are linked to the heart chakra, and lavender jadeite is used for gentle intuition and spiritual calm. Because fine pieces are so valued, jadeite is also treated as a symbol of earned status, a stone worn to honour achievement and character. Many people use it to cultivate patience and contentment. Physically it is traditionally associated with balance and long life, though it is a symbolic companion for wellbeing and never a replacement for care.
howToUse: Wear a jadeite bangle, bead or pendant daily so that the stone warms against your skin, a practice traditional in many Asian cultures. Keep a small piece in your bag or purse to invite steady good fortune. In meditation, hold a smooth stone over the heart and breathe slowly. A jadeite carving of a fish, coin or gourd can sit in the east or south-east of the home in feng shui practice. Pair it with green aventurine and clear quartz for a prosperity grid.
care: Jadeite is tough and water-safe, so wipe it with a soft damp cloth and dry it well. Avoid acids, bleach, ultrasonic cleaning and steam, which can harm impregnated B-grade stones. Cleanse with smoke, sound or moonlight, and avoid heat sources. Wearing it regularly is thought to improve its shine. Store in a soft pouch, and avoid contact with harder gems and with oils from creams or perfumes.
identify: Natural jadeite has a slightly granular, interlocking texture, and a fine, even colour. Translucent stones show a gentle glow. The trade grades stones A, B and C: A is natural, B is bleached and polymer-filled, and C is dyed. B and C can look similar to A when new. Fakes include dyed quartzite, serpentine, glass and so-called Malay jade. A gem laboratory report is essential for valuable bangles and cabochons.

faq.a: Jadeite is rarer, a little harder and can show richer, more translucent colour, so top-grade stones are far more valuable. Nephrite is tougher and has a long history, and both are genuine jade.

Imperial jade is the top colour grade of jadeite: an intense, even emerald green with good translucency. It is extremely rare and comes mainly from Myanmar, with prices that can reach very high levels.
Jadeite stands for luck, harmony, prosperity and dignified calm. In crystal practice it is linked with the heart chakra, and it is worn as a talisman for protection and wellbeing in daily life.
